dataset: GPM_MERGIR v1 — NCEP/CPC globally merged infrared brightness temperature, 4 km, 60 S .. 60 N, half-hourly

grid.band_note: rows [band_rows[0], band_rows[1]) of the source field above; IRTB_LAT_BAND chose them
grid.coordinates: lon = x0 + (col + 0.5) * dx, lat = y0 + (row + 0.5) * dy with dy POSITIVE; x0/y0 are the group's WEST and SOUTH edges

full_grid.note: the SOURCE field this band is cut from (3298 x 9896 for the real archive)

grid.no_tile_corners: a plain geographic grid: the affine rule above IS the lat/lon of every pixel and tile corner
grid.row_order: row 0 is the SOUTHERNMOST row — the source netCDF's own order, whose `lat` array ASCENDS. `grid_check` compares every file's lat/lon arrays against this affine rule and refuses on a mismatch

qc_policy: The merged IR field publishes no per-pixel quality flag; a pixel no satellite could see is the netCDF fill and becomes the layout's missing value 255. A kelvin outside [160, 414] — i.e. a stored value outside 0..254 — becomes missing and is COUNTED (`out_of_bounds`), never clipped: 160-330 K is the physical range of a merged IR field and anything past it is a broken file rather than a colder cloud. The store's unit is kelvin MINUS 160, the note's own encoding, and `tile_grid.json` says so in `channel_encoding`.
title: NCEP/CPC merged infrared brightness temperature (GPM_MERGIR v1), 4 km — cloud-top temperature; phase A is the tropics three-hourly
verified: 2026-09-18 from this sandbox (CMR only — a GES DISC .nc4 answers an anonymous GET with 302 to urs.earthdata.nasa.gov and then 401, so the BYTES are a hosted runner's job): the collection GPM_MERGIR v1 (C1432254058-GES_DISC, 1998-01-01 ->) and 2015-01-01's granules — 24 files, one an hour, `merg_2015010100_4km-pixel.nc4` .. `...23...`, 698.5 MB in total, 27.6-28.3 MB each — with each granule's own https .nc4 link read from its CMR entry. NOT MEASURED HERE, and what the runner probe settles: the file's internal variable layout (resolved against a candidate list, with the whole inventory written into plan.json), whether an hourly file really holds TWO time steps, the lat/lon axes against the declared affine grid, and the compressed bytes a tile and a frame.
